IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
INHERENT JURISDICTION
REVIEW PETITION (CRL) NO. 569 OF 2026 
IN
SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRL) NO. 11666 OF 2026
SUNITA         …      PETITIONER(S)
VERSUS
SANDEEP AND OTHERS                  … RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. We have perused the material available on record.
2. The petitioner/complainant has sought review of the order dated 30.06.2026
passed in S.L.P. (Crl.) No. 11666 of 2026, whereby the Special Leave Petition came to
be dismissed by this Court.
3. The challenge in the aforesaid Special Leave Petition was to the judgment and
order dated 30.03.2026 passed by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at
Chandigarh (Hereinafter referred to as “the High Court’), in CRM-M No. 34833 of
2023 (O&M), whereby the High Court quashed Criminal Complaint No. 193 of 2015,
the summoning order dated 06.02.2018 passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Gurugram, and the revisional order dated 01.06.2023 passed by the Additional
1

--- Page 392 ---
Sessions  Judge,  Gurugram, against  the  respondents/accused  for  the  offences
punishable under Sections 148, 149, 307, 452, 120B and 506 of the Indian Penal
Code, 1860 and Section 25 of the Arms Act, 1959.
4. It is seen that upon analysing the material available on record, the High Court
was of the opinion that the FIR was vague and omnibus and that no specific overt act
was attributed to the accused persons. The High Court further found that the conduct
of the petitioner in instituting the criminal proceedings against the accused was
intended to harass them rather than to pursue the remedies available in law.
Accordingly, the High Court quashed the criminal proceedings initiated against the
accused.
5. It is settled law that the High Court in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction, can
quash criminal proceedings where the allegations made in the FIR, even if taken at
their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not disclose the commission of the
alleged offence, or where continuation of the proceedings would amount to an abuse
of the process of law. This principle would equally apply where an offence under
Section 307 of the Indian Penal Code is alleged, if the requisite ingredients of the
offence are not disclosed from the allegations. 
6. Taking note of the aforesaid, this Court dismissed the Special Leave Petition.
We find no error apparent on the face of the record warranting review of the order
dated 30.06.2026 passed by us. 
2

--- Page 393 ---
7. Accordingly, the present Review Petition is dismissed. 
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of. 
    
……………………………………………………J.
    (R. MAHADEVAN)
……………………………………………………J.
    (ALOK ARADHE)
NEW DELHI;
SEPTEMBER 30, 2026.

2. The  present  petition  calls  in  question  the
correctness of the order  dated 04.05.2026 in MCRLC No.
20314/2026 passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at
Indore. By the said order, the prayer for anticipatory
bail of the petitioner was rejected in connection with FIR
No.  0448/2025  dated  17.09.2025  registered  at  Police
Station  Neelganga,  District  Ujjain  for  the  offences
punishable under Sections 69, 351(3) and 308(5) of the
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 and 66(E) and 66(A) of
the Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2000.
3. When the matter came up for hearing on 05.06.2026,
while  issuing  notice,  this  Court  had  granted  interim
protection to the petitioner.
4. We put to the learned counsel for the State whether
the  petitioner  is  cooperating  with  the  investigation?
Learned counsel for the State submits that the petitioner
had appeared before the investigation officer.
5. Keeping the overall facts and circumstances of the
case, and the fact that the petitioner has participated in
the investigation, we are inclined to confirm the order
dated  05.06.2026  granting  interim  protection  to  the
petitioner on the same terms.
6. With  the  above  observations,  the  Special  Leave
Petition is disposed of.

under the provisions of Rule 22 of the Madhya Pradesh
Municipalities (Colony Development) Rules, 2021, (for short,
‘the Rules, 2021’). In the said proceedings, the Collector-
cum-District Magistrate, District Guna directed the Chief
Municipal Officer, Nagar Palika, Guna to lodge an FIR or
file  a  complaint  against  the  petitioners  under  the
provisions of the Madhya Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1961.

Magistrate came to be challenged by way of writ petition
before the learned Single Judge of the High Court.

preferred by the petitioners.

learned Single Judge, the State preferred an appeal before
the Division Bench and the same came to be allowed.

date, no FIR or any complaint has been lodged.

is lodged, it shall be open for the petitioners to question

High Court, in accordance with law, on its own merits.

inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

5. By the impugned order dated 28.04.2026, the High

3. The appellant, who was arrayed as Accused No. 35 before

Terrorist & Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987 has
been preferred before this Court.

and the fact that the appeal is of the year 2026, and is

imposed upon the appellant, and grant bail to the appellant,
during the pendency of the appeal.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
Transfer Petition(s)(Criminal)  No(s).  737/2026
CHOPPA RAJASEKHAR & ORS.                           Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
KOTTHA BHANUSRI                                    Respondent(s)
O R D E R
1. The petitioner seeks transfer of case no. CC/1032/2022 pending 
at Ld. IV Additional Junior Civil Judge cum IV Additional JMFC, 
Mahabubnagar Court, Telangana to the Court of Judicial Magistrate 
First Class in Bangalore, Karnataka.
2. When confronted with the judgment ”M/s. Shri Sendhur Agro & Oil 
Industries vs. Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd. in TP (Crl.) No. 608/2024 
reported in 2025 INSC 328”, the learned counsel for petitioner is 
unable to respond satisfactorily. The relevant extract of the 
above-mentioned judgment is reproduced below:
“xxxx  xxxx  xxxx
65. For the purpose of transfer of any case or
proceedings under Section 406 of the Cr.P.C., the
case must fall within the ambit of the expression
“expedient  for  the  ends  of  justice”.  Mere
inconvenience or hardship that the accused may have
to face in travelling from Coimbatore to Chandigarh
would not fall within the expression “expedient for
the ends of justice”. The case must fall within any
of the five situations as narrated in para 49 of this
judgment.  It  is  always  open  for  the  petitioner
accused  to  pray  for  exemption  from  personal
appearance  or  request  the  Court  that  he  may  be
permitted to join the proceedings online.
xxxx xxxx xxxx”
1

--- Page 573 ---
3. In view of the above, it is obvious that inconvenience alone 
cannot be the lone ground (as herein), for seeking transfer of 
criminal case.
4. In accordance with the above, there is no case made out. The 
transfer petition is accordingly dismissed.

1

--- Page 594 ---
petitioner by the high Court in his appeal which was
pending consideration at the time when this Special Leave
Petition was preferred.
2. Despite the above, the  Special Leave Petition  was
kept pending, noticing that the petitioner was behind bars
for more than 21 years, and the appeal has been pending
consideration for more than 15 years.
3. This  Court,  therefore,  sought  reports  from  the
concerned High Court as to the steps taken for the disposal
of appeals, where the accused are suffering incarceration
for a long period of time.
4. Reports were submitted to this Court from time to
time, and today, Mr. Tanmaya Agarwal, learned standing
counsel for the High Court of Allahabad, placed before us
the  present  status  report  regarding  the  pendency  of
criminal appeals in the main seat of the Allahabad High
Court as well as at the Lucknow Bench.
5. Having perused the status report, it appears that
steps have been taken for the disposal of such appeals,
where the convicts have been languishing in jail for a
considerable period of time.
6. We  hope  that  this  effort  will  continue  and
preference shall be given to the hearing of such appeals
where the convicts are in jail for more than 15 years, to
begin with, and thereafter to appeals where the convicts
are in jail for more than 10 years.

committed an act of forgery.

special leave petition stands disposed of with a direction

For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, we notice
that the learned Single Judge vide order dated 27.02.2020 after having
considered the rival contentions and after evaluating the documents tendered
by both the parties has arrived at the following conclusion:
“Mr. Vaisya, learned advocate appearing for the respondents has
produced before this Court an extract of a bank statement from which it
appears that the pension was disbursed in favour of the petitioner’s father
till the month of January, 2009 and family pension was disbursed in favour
of the petitioner’s mother on and from the month of June, 2009 to October,
2009. Though  there is no  statement  pertaining to the period from
February, 2009 till May, 2009, it appears that in the month of June, 2009
1

--- Page 1045 ---
the account of the petitioner’s mother was credited with an amount of
Rs.22,908/-.”
2. In the background of the aforesaid finding recorded and in light of bank
statement produced by the respondent(s), we do not see any justification for
the  petitioner  to make  a claim for family  pension  from  25.12.2008  to
02.10.2009. However, prima facie, at this juncture, we are of the view that the
petitioner would be entitled for the family pension from 02.10.2009 till April,
2016, since there is no dispute to the fact that from 01.05.2016 till 27.11.2018
(till the date of petitioner secured an employment), he was paid the pension.
Hence, issue notice both on the application for condonation of delay and on the
petition for the limited purpose of examining as to why the petitioner has been
deprived of the family pension from 02.10.2009 till April, 2016, returnable
within six weeks.

The appellant herein is the first accused (A1) and has been
convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 148 and 302 of
the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, “IPC”) by the trial Court
and sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life, along with fine and
default stipulations. The judgment of conviction and order on
sentence rendered by the Trial Court have  been confirmed by the
High Court vide the impugned judgment and order. Aggrieved by the
same, the appellant is before this Court.
Taking into consideration the fact that the appellant has
undergone incarceration for more than a period of ten years, we are
inclined to suspend the sentence imposed on the appellant and grant
him bail, during the pendency of the present appeal.
Accordingly, the sentence imposed upon the appellant stands
suspended, and the appellant shall be released on bail during the
pendency of the present appeal, subject to the terms and conditions
as may be imposed by the concerned Trial Court.
List the appeal for hearing in its due course.
In the meantime, call for the records from the Courts below.

preferred  by  the  Petitioner  herein  seeking  to  challenge  the
legality and validity of the show cause notice on the ground that
the petitioner has an alternative efficacious remedy of appeal.  
3. We grant six weeks time to the petitioner to prefer an
appropriate statutory appeal before the appellate authority and
raise all contentions available to him in law including the fact
that no adequate opportunity of hearing was given at the time of
adjudication of the show cause notice.
4. With the aforesaid, the Special Leave Petition stands disposed
of.
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
(CHANDRESH)                                     (POOJA SHARMA)

UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
O R D E R
1. We have considered the submissions at the Bar.  We note
that the petitioner was in custody earlier and having been
released on bail during COVID, misused such liberty and was
finally taken into custody on 26.04.2020.  Noting his conduct,
this  Court,  by  an  earlier  order  dated  07.02.2024,  had
restricted the right of the petitioner to seek bail only
before this Court. 
1

--- Page 1323 ---
2. Given the situation, petitioner has approached us for
grant of bail in the present application.
3. The petitioner is in custody for more than 2 ½ years, and
investigation is complete. Petitioner is charged with offences
which carry a maximum sentence of seven years. Keeping in mind
the aforesaid facts, and the fact that there is no possibility
of conclusion of trial in the near future, we are of the
opinion  further  detention  of  the  petitioner  would  be
essentially punitive in nature.
4. Accordingly,  we  direct  that  the  petitioner  may  be
enlarged on bail on furnishing bond(s) to the satisfaction of
the jurisdictional Magistrate and subject to such terms and
conditions as the said Court may deem fit and proper to
impose.
5. Miscellaneous  Application  stands  disposed  of,  with
pending application(s), if any.

pending in Allahabad High Court. The writ was instituted in 2022

in Diary No. 23212/2023 passed by the Supreme Court of India]
PRAVEEN SRIVASTAV                                Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
STATE OF NCT OF DELHI                            Respondent(s)
 
Date : 01-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE V. MOHANA
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Shakti Kanta Pattanaik- 2781, AOR
                   Mr. Vikrant Sharma, Adv.
                   Mr. Bikash Vishwakarma, Adv.
                   Mr. Dhirendra Kumar, Adv.
                                      
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Kanakamedala Ravindra Kumar, ASG
Mr. Devraj Bhattacharjee, Adv. 
UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
O R D E R
1. We have considered the submissions at the Bar.  We note
that the petitioner was in custody earlier and having been
released on bail during COVID, misused such liberty and was
finally taken into custody on 26.04.2020.  Noting his conduct,
this  Court,  by  an  earlier  order  dated  07.02.2024,  had
restricted the right of the petitioner to seek bail only
before this Court. 
1

--- Page 1377 ---
2. Given the situation, petitioner has approached us for
grant of bail in the present application.
3. The petitioner is in custody for more than 2 ½ years, and
investigation is complete. Petitioner is charged with offences
which carry a maximum sentence of seven years. Keeping in mind
the aforesaid facts, and the fact that there is no possibility
of conclusion of trial in the near future, we are of the
opinion  further  detention  of  the  petitioner  would  be
essentially punitive in nature.
4. Accordingly,  we  direct  that  the  petitioner  may  be
enlarged on bail on furnishing bond(s) to the satisfaction of
the jurisdictional Magistrate and subject to such terms and
conditions as the said Court may deem fit and proper to
impose.
5. I.A.  No.96879/2026  is  allowed  and  the  Miscellaneous
Application stands disposed of, with pending application(s),
if any.
(NITIN TALREJA)                        (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                     DY. REGISTRAR
